title: Formed in Thine Image Bright
description: Formed in Thine Image Bright in Tonic Solfa to QUAM DILECTA, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sixes (6.6.6.6), and this page sets them to QUAM DILECTA; any other Sixes tune fits them as well.
underlay: Formed in Thine i-mage bright, With glo-ry on my head, I lived with-in Thy light, And on Thy boun-ty fed.

lines: Dark came the night of sin,
Gone was the joy of earth.
Yea, though the prayer be vain,
Now will I lift mine eyes,
Came there a voice to me,
Up from my woes I'll rise,

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to QUAM DILECTA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
